blocks.content: ETHAN
I did not follow her to the park.

I want to be clear about that. The park had good light. The archway had a nice shape. The broken fountain was interesting in a compositionally useful way — the kind of decay that looks intentional in a painting. These were all legitimate artistic reasons.
None of them explain why I positioned my easel with a direct sightline to that specific bench.
I'm a work in progress.

I set up around noon. Headphones in, nothing playing — the universal signal for please don't talk to me. First layer came down fast: sky, trees, stone, water. I was moving into detail when a voice behind me said:

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: That fountain looks better in your painting than it does in real life.
I startled hard enough to almost drag my brush across the canvas.
I turned around.
Red hair. Green jacket. Purple dinosaur. Her.
My brain, which is generally functional, chose this exact moment to go completely offline.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: Uh.
Excellent. Very smooth.

Up close she was the kind of person who looked real in a way that made it harder, not easier — freckle near one cheekbone, a smudge of ink on one finger, wind had pulled her hair across her face and she had zero interest in fixing it. She leaned toward the canvas with actual curiosity, like she wasn't performing it, and I became very aware that I had centered the bench where she'd been sitting directly in the middle of the composition.

As a painter, I notice things and put them in pictures. This is my whole job. I'm mentioning it because it means the bench being there was intentional, and I would very much like to not have that conversation.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: I didn't mean to scare you.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: You didn't.
She looked at the brush. Then at the blue streak now across my knuckle.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: You sure?

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: Oh.
She smiled. The same one from across the street, except now I was close enough to see it properly and that was significantly worse for my ability to function.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: I'm Cassandra.
I stared for half a second too long before remembering that names are something people exchange.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: Ethan.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: Ethan the painter.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: I guess.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: You guess?

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: I mean — technically, yes.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: Technically a painter?

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: That sounded less dumb in my head.
